evidence.notes: All three builds use the same domain-appropriate composition: a ward capacity strip that doubles as a filter, a grouped triage queue and an inspector. All have no contract changes, clean axe results, no overflow and GET-only loads, and none has a critical failure. Y is the most complete on governed actions and state truthfulness: two-step impact previews, timestamped server-confirmed receipts, typed failure messages, a staleness banner and careful focus management. Its weak spot is that the ward cards stack vertically on mobile and push the queue down. Z nearly matches Y on action governance and handles mobile better (2x2 tiles), but it exposes MRNs in every queue row and groups by status only, so an overdue escalated alert sinks to the bottom. X has the best triage grouping (overdue first regardless of status) and a good mobile ward carousel. Its acknowledge action is a single click with no impact preview, and its success receipt has no timestamp. Overall Y ranks slightly ahead of X and Z, which are close to each other.

scorer_rationale.task_hierarchy: The queue dominates, with a 'past due / without owner' summary and a 'Needs attention only' toggle. Grouping is by status only (Needs action = open), so the overdue escalated AL-2031 sinks to the bottom of 'In progress' (primary-1440.png).
scorer_rationale.domain_adaptation: The capacity strip ('No beds free', 'Short N beds', 'N free') and handoff history fit the domain. But every queue row shows the MRN (AlertQueue.tsx: `{a.patientRef && {a.patientRef}}`), which goes against the expectation to expose patient-sensitive detail only where needed.
scorer_rationale.contract_preservation: No contract files changed. The route becomes /alerts/* but both paths still resolve, and test IDs, server filters and the original test are kept.
scorer_rationale.interaction_state: Has skeletons, filtered vs unfiltered empty states, errors with Retry, 404, 'could not refresh — showing the last loaded list', and 409 'Load latest version' that keeps the draft. 403 and network errors say nothing was changed, and the receipt is server-confirmed with time and new owner.
scorer_rationale.responsive: No overflow. At 375 the ward tiles form a compact 2x2 grid, so the queue stays reachable. Below 960 the detail is full screen with 'Back to queue' and focus returns to the row. verify reports 1 small target.
scorer_rationale.accessibility: axe is clean, 29/29 focus-visible stops, urgency uses a distinct icon shape plus text, and Escape cancels forms. The heading is focused on every detail load, including split view, which takes focus away from the queue on desktop.
scorer_rationale.visual_consistency: Coherent and calm. Rows are full cards with coloured edges, a little heavier than Y.
scorer_rationale.maintainability: Console, detail, queue and capacity are separated, and format.ts has unit tests. AlertDetailPanel.tsx is a 440-line file holding several forms.
scorer_rationale.ai_governance: Inline confirmation forms state the impact ('Ownership transfers to X'), escalate requires a target and a reason, and the receipt reads 'confirmed by the server at HH:MM' and is dismissible.

justified_patterns: focus returns to the originating row on mobile
suspicious_patterns: MRNs shown in every queue row without a task need
ward tiles resemble a KPI row (justified by pressure labels)

strengths: governed action flow with impact and receipt
unit tests for triage and pressure logic
the refresh spinner is disabled under reduced motion
defects: patient MRNs exposed in queue rows
an overdue escalated alert is grouped as 'In progress' at the bottom
the heading is focused on every detail load in split view
